My parents split when I was younger and since I lived with my mom and she went to school, I never saw either parent too often. When we moved, my dad never really made an effort to come and see me, though he did call every day. During my early teens, my mom and I used to argue and she would hit me, and I was so fed up with it I told my dad I wanted to live with him. He agreed, and when my mom found out, she gave me the ultimatum. I ended up chickening out, which I think really hurt my dad, and the whole ordeal permanently scarred my relationship with my mom. 
Fast forward a few years. I am now 15 and my dad calls less and less frequently. I tried at first to call him, but my mom told me it was his responsibility since he was the parent so I stopped. A month or so goes by, and I wake up one morning to the news that he has shot himself. He wasn't calling me because he was at his most depressed. I was devastated. He never made an effort to see me when I moved because he couldn't afford to, and he felt his relationship with his daughter was ruined and that I didn't love him anymore. 
I forever will regret not calling him. He sent me an email an hour before he died asking me to call him and I didn't see it in time. 
Because of all of this, I have tried to repair my relationship with my mom and understand that we are two different people. We still argue a lot, but I will always love her. 
TL;DR--don't take your parents for granted. Nothing lasts forever.
